lines.trans: Heard you got robbed by your own staff. Man, you really are hilarious.
It's not funny—investigate seriously! I'm completely out of time here!
You lend me the cash! You've got money shaken down from the yakuza—I'll expose you!
Extorting a police detective now? You really have lost your mind.
Kawada and Toshi—those two are working together now. Bet you didn't know.
If you want to borrow a big lump sum, you know the perfect guy—an old acquaintance of yours.
I'm glad you came to lean on me even after I ended up in this wheelchair.

meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: この映画はとても面白いです。
何か面白い話はありませんか。
examples.trans: Do you have any interesting stories?

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Intensifies the following adverb or verb, as in もっとちゃんと見て.

examples.text: もっと近くで見てください。
もっとゆっくり話してください。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Casual counterpart of こちら.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Everyday noun for time on the clock or a dedicated stretch of time.

examples.text: まだ少し時間があります。
examples.trans: There is still a little time.

examples.text: 楽しい時間をありがとう。
examples.trans: Thank you for the fun time.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: お前が貸せ。ヤクザから巻き上げた金があるだろ、バラすぞ。

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 刑事を恐喝してるのか？お前いよいよぶっ壊れてるな。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 今のこの高ぶった感情のまま、もう一本撮らせてくれ。
examples.trans: While your emotions are still running this high, let me shoot one more scene.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.note: Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

examples.text: ウソじゃないよ。お前は風邪ひくんじゃないよ。
examples.trans: It's not a lie. Don't you go catching a cold.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: know; find out; be aware of
meanings.note: Godan verb; state of knowing is 知っている.

examples.text: 彼の電話番号を知っていますか。
examples.trans: Do you know his phone number?

examples.text: 本当の理由を知りたい。
examples.trans: I want to know the real reason.

meanings.note: Colloquial conjunction built from だ + たら.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Godan verb; 持ってくる means 'bring'.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.
